payload.claim:
Recorded as the measurable anchor for a memory-cycle view whose vehicle may be LKOR (MSCI Korea 20/35, roughly 55% Samsung Electronics, SK hynix and SK Square) or SK hynix itself. Korean listings and ETFs are outside the archive, so Micron's gross margin carries the scoreable claim. The open question is not FY2027, which is largely contracted (over 75% of FY2027 output committed; agreements covering over 35% of revenue through 2030; SK hynix: over half of 2027-28 capacity), but how fast pricing normalises once 2028-29 capacity lands.
- Upgrade case: DRAM contract prices still rising into 2H 2027; FY2028 agreements extended at fixed prices; Samsung and SK hynix do not raise 2028 capex further; physical-AI / world-model demand shows up in orders.
- Downgrade case: DRAM contract prices flat-to-down before mid-2028; industry 2028 capex raised while price growth decelerates; hyperscalers defer 2027 (not only 2028) capex, or long-term agreements are renegotiated; CXMT qualifies HBM at scale or wins Apple volume; US data-center permitting restrictions that cut 2027 build volumes.
- Context on the day: MU closed at $656.39 on 5 Nov 2026 after a 17.5% one-day fall (SOX -12%) on US midterm data-center policy fears and a reported Taiwan fab suspension; no change to orders or pricing was reported.

prediction.reasoning: FY2026 GAAP gross margin was 80.7%, and management guides sequential revenue growth in every quarter of FY2027 with supply 'much tighter' in calendar 2027-28. Most new cleanroom capacity (Micron ID1 mid-2027 and ID2 end-2028, SK hynix Yongin, CXMT adding about 100k wafers/month a year) ships after FY2028 ends in August 2028. Contract-price growth is already decelerating, so the margin should come off the peak, but falling below 70% inside FY2028 would need price per bit to drop by roughly a third against rising depreciation within two years. This is where I part from the price: at about 4x FY2027 EPS the market prices a fast normalisation; I expect it to arrive later than FY2028.
